errors.oidc_exchange_failed: The provider did not confirm the sign-in. Are client ID and secret right?
errors.oidc_issuer_mismatch: The provider names itself with a different address than the one entered.

errors.public_url_invalid: Only scheme and host, like https://nexsift.example.com.
errors.rule_name: The rule needs a name, at most 120 characters.
errors.rule_no_action: The rule needs at least one effect under "Then".
errors.rule_no_condition: The rule needs at least one condition.
errors.rule_regex: The pattern is not a valid regular expression.
errors.rule_value: Every condition needs a value, at most 300 characters.
errors.sender_host_invalid: Only a host name or an IP address, like 192.168.1.10, without a port.
errors.target_field_missing: A required field is still missing for this target ({{field}}).
errors.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Please try again in {{retry_after}} seconds.
errors.url_invalid: The address must start with http:// or https://.

inbox.emptyHint: New messages show up here on their own, without reloading.

fact.neverPush: This kind of message never goes to the phone (rule).
fact.noRule: No rule; the level came from the sender.
fact.notPushedWhy: Only what reaches a target's minimum level goes to the phone. This one is {{priority}}.
fact.pushHelp: When nexsift sends something to the phone is decided by the targets (from which level) and the push behaviour (at once, bundled or never). Both are under Rules.
fact.rule: Why it was sorted like this
fact.ruleHelp: Rules decide level, bundling and push. These are all the ones that applied to this message.
fact.throttledHelp: When a source sends more messages per minute than allowed (under Rules, Defaults), nexsift only counts the rest. That keeps the inbox usable when a container runs amok.
fact.throttledText: Above the limit messages are only counted, not stored and never forwarded.

inbox.markAllRead: Mark everything in this view as read
inbox.muted: {{name}} is muted for an hour. Messages keep arriving, only nothing goes to the phone.
inbox.noHitsHint: The search looks at title and text of all messages in this view.
inbox.nothingSelected: Pick a message on the left
inbox.nothingYet: The open message shows up here once the first one is in.
inbox.olderGone_one: One older message of this bundle is not shown here any more.
inbox.olderGone_other: {{count}} older messages of this bundle are not shown here any more.
inbox.onlyThisSource: Show only messages of this source
inbox.setUpPhone: No target for the phone yet? This way.
inbox.sourcesHelp: Every sender that reports to nexsift is a source. A click filters the inbox to it. A yellow warning sign means its format was not recognized lately.
inbox.unrecognizedHelp: nexsift knows this sender's format, but this message looked different. It is complete anyway, only without extras like bundling or the all-clear. "Raw data" shows exactly what arrived.

viewHelp.crit: Critical problems without an all-clear yet. Key 3.
viewHelp.unread: Only what you have not opened yet. Key 2.

languages.coverageHint: Share of texts that are translated. The rest shows in English.

error.badCode: The _meta block needs a valid language code, such as fr, pt-BR or sr-Latn.
error.badLabel: The _meta block needs a short label, three characters at most.
error.badName: The _meta block needs the name of the language, 40 characters at most.
error.builtInCode: German and English are built in and cannot be replaced. Please choose another language code.
error.noMeta: The _meta block is missing. The template is the easiest start.
error.noTexts: The file contains not a single usable text.
error.notJson: This is not a valid JSON file.

languages.intro: Upload your own translations. What is missing shows in English, so a half-done translation already works.

mode.addHint: The new texts are added or replace those with the same key, everything else stays. Right for a file with the missing texts.
mode.replaceHint: The old version is dropped, only this file counts.

reason.placeholders: placeholders like {{example}} do not match English

report.missing_one: One text is missing and shows in English.
report.missing_other: {{count}} texts are missing and show in English.
report.rejected_one: One text was not taken, it shows in English.
report.rejected_other: {{count}} texts were not taken, they show in English.
report.title: Check {{name}}
report.unknown_one: One key is unknown and ignored.

step.one: Download the template. It holds every text in English and the _meta block on top.
step.three: Upload it here. nexsift checks the file and shows what is missing before anything is stored.
step.two: Translate the texts, fill in code, name and label in the _meta block. Leave placeholders like {{example}} as they are.

live.offHelp: The live connection to the server is down right now. It comes back on its own.
live.onHelp: New messages show up at once, without reloading.

login.forgot: Forgot the password? Run in the container:
login.lead: Sign in to see your inbox.
login.name: Name
login.providerFailed: The sign-in through the provider did not work.
login.title: Sign in

hint.immediate: The first critical event of a topic goes out at once. More are counted quietly; at the end of the bundle window a follow-up comes if there were more.
hint.never: Stays in the inbox, never goes to the phone.
hint.single: Every event on its own, at once. Only throttling and the storm guard slow it down.
hint.window: A single push at the end of the bundle window, with the count. Quieter, but up to one window later.

builtInName.keywordsCritical: Words for failures make it critical
builtInName.keywordsWarning: Words for trouble make it a warning
builtInName.paperless: Paperless: bundle new documents, never push them
builtInName.sshd: sshd: failed sign-ins in one line
builtInName.watchtower: Watchtower: bundle updates, never push them

defaults.help: These values hold as long as no rule says otherwise.
defaults.intro: What applies when no rule says otherwise.
defaults.pushHelp: How critical messages reach the phone. "At once, then bundle quietly" is right for nearly everyone.
defaults.throttleHelp: When a source sends more than this many messages per minute, nexsift only counts the rest. Protects against endless loops.
defaults.title: Defaults
defaults.windowHelp: What arrives within this time shares a line: all info messages of a source together as routine, warnings and critical ones per subject. An open critical problem stays one line until it is resolved.

editor.builtInNote: nexsift brought this rule along. You can change it, switch it off or delete it.
editor.dropHint: The message is counted but not stored. For noise nobody wants to read.
editor.groupKeyHelp: Messages with the same key share a line. Values from the message in curly braces, like vm-{vmid}. Leave empty: nexsift puts a source's info messages together, and warnings with the same title.
editor.name: Name
editor.nameHelp: What the rule is for, in your words. The name shows on every message it hits.
editor.priorityHelp: Info stays quiet, warning is yellow, critical is red and goes to the phone if a target wants it.
editor.pushHelp: Overrides the default push behaviour for these messages.
editor.resolvesHelp: When the rule hits, the message closes the open problem with this bundle key instead of opening a line of its own. Like: rule on "is UP", all-clear for monitor-{monitor}.
editor.sourceHelp: Only for messages of this source, or for all.
editor.thenHelp: What happens with a matching message. Several rules can work together: for every effect the topmost rule that sets it wins.
editor.titleTemplateHelp: What the line in the inbox is called. {count} becomes the number, like: Watchtower: {count} containers updated.
editor.whenHelp: All conditions must hold. Upper and lower case do not matter.
editor.wordHint: "whole word" only hits whole words, so not "0 errors" for ERROR. Several words with a vertical bar: FAIL|ERROR.

rules.lead: What matters how much, what belongs together and what may reach the phone.

list.help: Rules are checked top to bottom. All matching ones apply; for every effect the topmost wins. The arrows change the order, the switch turns a rule off without deleting it.
list.intro: All matching rules apply, top to bottom. For every effect the topmost wins.
list.title: Rules

storm.help: When the power goes, twenty services report at once. Instead of twenty pushes one summary comes when the wave is over. The inbox still shows everything on its own.
storm.hint: When many services fail at once, one summary comes instead of twenty pushes.
storm.title: Storm guard across all sources

tester.help: Type a message the way a sender would send it. nexsift shows which rules apply and what comes out. Nothing lands in the inbox.
tester.intro: Try a message before it arrives.
tester.none: No rule matches. The level then comes from the sender.
tester.title: Try a rule

rules.title: Rules

about.reset: Forgot the password and no provider set up? Run on the server:
about.title: About nexsift

account.emailHelp: nexsift recognizes you by this address when you sign in through authentik or another provider. The provider must confirm it.
account.emailHint: For signing in through a provider.
account.help: nexsift has exactly one account. Other browsers are signed out when the password changes.
account.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other browsers are signed out.
account.title: Account

authentik.blueprint: Rather without a token: blueprint file
authentik.blueprintHelp: A YAML file for authentik's blueprint import. It creates the same as the button. Then enter client ID and secret below under "Other provider".
authentik.done: authentik is set up. You no longer need the token; best delete it in authentik right away. The button shows on the sign-in page from the next sign-out.
authentik.failed: The setup stopped. The red line says where. Fix it and simply run it again.
authentik.help: The button creates provider, application, signing key and the mapping for email_verified in authentik and fills everything into nexsift. A second run updates instead of creating duplicates.
authentik.lead: nexsift creates everything in authentik itself. It needs an API token once for that.

step.filled: Client ID and secret filled into nexsift

authentik.title: Sign in with authentik
authentik.tokenHelp: In authentik: Directory, Tokens and App passwords, Create, intent "API Token". The user needs admin rights.
authentik.tokenHint: nexsift uses it once and does not store it.
authentik.urlHelp: As nexsift reaches authentik, like https://auth.example.com. Without /application at the end.

other.help: For Keycloak, Pocket ID, Authelia, Zitadel and every other one with OpenID Connect. Create an application at the provider, enter the redirect address shown below, then issuer, client ID and secret here.
other.issuerHelp: The address under which the provider serves /.well-known/openid-configuration, without that part.
other.lead: Keycloak, Pocket ID, Authelia, Zitadel and every other one with OpenID Connect.
other.providerNameHelp: Shows on the sign-in page: "Sign in with …".
other.redirectHelp: Enter this address at the provider as redirect URI. It follows the public address under "Sign-in".
other.removed: Provider removed. Sign-in with a password is on again.
other.title: Other provider

retention.archiveHelp: Archived messages are deleted after this many days.
retention.eventsHelp: Messages in the inbox are deleted after this many days without news. An open critical problem always stays.
retention.help: Cleaning up happens every five minutes in the background.
retention.lead: What gets deleted after that. Open critical problems always stay.
retention.rawHelp: Raw data is what the sender sent word for word. Useful while setting up, rarely afterwards. The message itself stays.
retention.title: Retention

signin.help: The public address is where the sign-in provider sends you back to. The address for senders goes into the setup hints of the sources.
signin.lead: Address to the outside and sign-in with a password.
signin.passwordHelp: Off: only through the provider. For emergencies a command in the container resets the password and switches the password sign-in back on.
signin.passwordNeedsProvider: Set up a provider first; then this can be switched off.
signin.publicUrlHelp: Behind a reverse proxy, the address you type into the browser. Empty: nexsift takes the address of the request.
signin.senderHostHelp: The address routers, the NAS, Proxmox and the like reach nexsift by. It goes into every setup hint. Needed once nexsift sits behind a reverse proxy: syslog, email and the Gotify and ntfy doors do not go through the proxy. Empty: nexsift takes the public address.
signin.senderHostHint: Like 192.168.1.10 or nas.home.arpa, without a port.
signin.title: Sign-in and address

setup.emailHelp: Only needed if you want to sign in through authentik or another provider later. Can be added in the settings any time.
setup.emailHint: For signing in through authentik and the like. Can be changed later.
setup.lead: Welcome. nexsift gathers your homelab's messages in one place, bundles the noise and only pushes what matters to your phone. First the account you sign in with.
setup.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
setup.name: Name
setup.nameHelp: Your sign-in name. Lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes.
setup.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. A sentence is easier to remember than special characters.
setup.title: Set up nexsift
setup.tooShort: Still too short: at least 12 characters.

shortcuts.mute: Mute the source for an hour
shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts

sources.deleteText: The source, all its messages and its own rules are deleted. The sender gets a refusal from then on. This cannot be undone.

dialog.arrived: The first message has arrived. Everything is set up right.
dialog.hostnameHelp: Every syslog line names the machine it comes from. Enter that here. If you do not know it: just let the device send; nexsift lists unknown senders at the top of this page.
dialog.hostnameHint: As the device names itself in syslog, like gw or router. Its IP address if nothing else.
dialog.knownHelp: nexsift knows what messages from these services look like. Outages and all-clears are paired, updates bundled, important things recognized. The small gray note says which way the service reports.
dialog.knownLead: The guide follows their settings step by step.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameHelp: What the source is called in the inbox. Free to choose, can be changed later.
dialog.nameLead: After creating it, nexsift shows what to enter on the device.
dialog.ownKey: The sender already uses "{{key}}". The new source takes exactly that; nothing changes at the sender.
dialog.pickLead: Every device reports in its own way. Pick what should report. nexsift then shows you exactly the fields to fill in over there, with values to copy.
dialog.viaName: The devices are given the name {{host}} here. If it leads to a reverse proxy or out to the internet, their messages will not arrive. Enter the address nexsift has at home, usually the server's IP:
dialog.viaNameLater: Applies to all sources. Change it later under Settings, Sign-in and address.
dialog.viaOutside: {{host}} leads to {{address}}, an address on the internet. The devices end up at the router, not at nexsift, even if the name is blocked from outside: the router only forwards the reverse proxy's port. Enter the server's IP at home:
dialog.waiting: Waiting for the first message. Set up the sender and trigger a test message there.
dialog.waysHelp: nexsift understands all of these ways. The order is a recommendation: a webhook carries the most, almost every device can send email. The message arrives either way.
dialog.waysLead: Look in your device's notification settings for which of these it offers. Take the topmost one it knows.
dialog.waysTitle: Not listed? Then by the way it reports

sources.explain: Every service that reports to nexsift is a source. nexsift acts as the service the sender already knows (Gotify, ntfy, Discord, email, syslog). You only enter nexsift's address in the sender. The lines to copy are under "Set up" at every source.

field.test: To try it in a terminal

sources.lead: Who reports, and by which way.

lineHint.curlTest: Sends a test message. It shows up in the inbox at once.
lineHint.discordUrl: Enter it where the Discord webhook address would go.
lineHint.kumaPreset: In Uptime Kuma, choose the preset "application/json" under "Request Body".
lineHint.paperlessBody: Take it exactly like this. Paperless fills the double curly braces itself, and a title with quotes still arrives intact.
lineHint.proxmoxBody: Proxmox fills the placeholders in double curly braces itself.
lineHint.proxmoxNoHeader: No header is needed. Delete the empty header row in Proxmox with the bin icon, otherwise it will not save. Leave secrets empty.
lineHint.recipient: The name before the @ ties the mail to this source. The domain does not matter.
lineHint.sender: Anything; many devices just want some address here.
lineHint.shoutrrrGeneric: Only for programs that expect addresses like gotify:// or discord:// (shoutrrr). Everything else takes the address above.
lineHint.synologyBody: Leave the parameter "text" in the body as it is.
lineHint.syslogHostname: The device must carry this name in its syslog lines.
lineHint.watchtowerEnv: Then restart the Watchtower container. The address holds the token, so do not pass it on.

sources.muteHelp: Messages keep arriving, only nothing goes to the phone.
sources.neverHeard: No message yet. "Set up" shows what to enter in the sender.
sources.noneHint: Create the first one. The dialog shows exactly what to enter in the sender.

ports.discord: Discord webhooks only work where the full address is entered (Uptime Kuma, Proxmox). Watchtower and other shoutrrr tools send to discord.com, fixed. Use the Gotify way there.
ports.help: nexsift opens several doors, each speaks like the service a sender expects. The numbers are the ports on your server. Struck through: this door is switched off.
ports.lead: On these ports nexsift takes messages.
ports.title: Entrances

discord.name: Discord webhook
discord.short: For programs that can only report to Discord. nexsift's address goes where Discord's would.

steps.s1: In the program, open the Discord notification.
steps.s2: Enter the address from here in the field for the Discord webhook URL.

email.name: Email
email.short: For devices that can only send mail, like a UPS, a printer or an older router.

steps.s1: On the device, open the mail notification (often "SMTP" or "Mail server").
steps.s2: Enter SMTP server, port and recipient from here. Turn off sign-in and encryption (SSL/TLS).
steps.s3: As the sender, any address, if the device asks for one.

gotify.name: Gotify
gotify.short: For programs that can report to a Gotify server. nexsift acts as one.

steps.s1: In the program, choose Gotify as the notification.
steps.s2: Enter server and token (sometimes "app token") from here.

homeassistant.name: Home Assistant
homeassistant.short: Your own messages from automations, through the ntfy integration.

steps.s1: In Home Assistant: Settings, Devices and services, Add integration, "ntfy".
steps.s2: The server address from here, without sign-in.
steps.s3: Add the topic from here. Then use "notify.send_message" in automations.

ntfy.name: ntfy
ntfy.short: For programs that can report to an ntfy server. nexsift acts as one.

steps.s1: In the program, choose ntfy as the notification.
steps.s2: As the server the address from here, as the topic the one from here. No sign-in.

paperless.name: Paperless-ngx
paperless.short: New documents, bundled, not to the phone.

steps.s1: In Paperless: Workflows, "Add Workflow". Any name, like nexsift.
steps.s2: Under Triggers: "Add Trigger", trigger type "Document Added".
steps.s4: Webhook url from here. Leave both "Use parameters for webhook body" and "Send webhook payload as JSON" off. The body from here into "Webhook body".
steps.s5: Save and upload a document. nexsift collects new documents in one line, none of them go to the phone.

proxmox.name: Proxmox VE
proxmox.short: Backups, replication, updates and failures, through Proxmox' webhook.

steps.s1: In Proxmox: Datacenter, Notifications, Add under Notification Targets, "Webhook".
steps.s2: Any endpoint name, like nexsift. Method POST and the address from here.
steps.s3: Delete the empty header row with the bin icon; no header is needed. Paste the body from here into Body.
steps.s4: Add. Check with Test on the target that it arrives.
steps.s5: Important: Test goes straight to the target, real notifications go through matchers. Open the default-matcher under Notification Matchers and also tick nexsift under Targets to notify. Otherwise backups and updates never arrive.

synology.name: Synology
synology.short: DSM warnings through its built-in webhook. The NAS' mail stays as it is.

steps.s1: In DSM: Control Panel, Notification, tab "Webhooks", Add.
steps.s2: Provider "Custom", rule "All". nexsift sorts out what matters itself.
steps.s3: Any provider name, like nexsift. Any subject. Webhook URL from here. Tick "Send notifications in English": nexsift recognizes problems by English words like failed or degraded.
steps.s4: Next: HTTP method POST, Content-Type application/json. Leave the parameter "text" in the body as it is; DSM puts the message there.

syslog.name: Syslog
syslog.short: For routers, switches and firewalls. On the device usually "Remote syslog" or "Syslog server".

steps.s1: On the device, find "Remote syslog" or "Syslog server" and turn it on.
steps.s2: Enter server and port from here, protocol UDP.
steps.s3: nexsift matches the lines by the hostname the device sends along. If nothing arrives, the right name shows at the top of this page under unknown senders.

ups.name: UPS, router, printer (email)
ups.short: For devices that can only send mail.

steps.s1: Open the mail notification in the device.
steps.s2: Enter SMTP server, port and recipient from here, no sign-in and no SSL.

steps.s1: In Uptime Kuma: Settings, Notifications, Setup notification, type "Webhook".
steps.s3: Press "Test", then switch it on for the monitors you want.

watchtower.name: Watchtower
watchtower.short: Container updates, bundled into one line, never to the phone.

steps.s1: Put the line below into the environment of the Watchtower container.
steps.s2: Restart Watchtower. The updates come with its next run.

webhook.name: Webhook
webhook.short: Often called "Webhook", "HTTP" or "Custom" on the device. Also for your own scripts.

steps.s1: On the device, choose the "Webhook" notification (sometimes "HTTP request" or "Custom").
steps.s2: Enter the address from here, method POST.
steps.s3: If the body can be set: JSON with title, message and priority (info, warning or critical). If it cannot: no matter, nexsift takes what comes.
steps.s4: Send a test message. It shows up below as soon as it arrives.

sources.renewConfirm: The old token stops working at once. Go on?
sources.renewHelp: In case the token ended up where it does not belong. Then enter the new line in the sender.
sources.renewed: New token. Now enter it in the sender.

strangers.help: These senders already send to nexsift, but no source fits: usually a typo or a device that names itself differently than expected. One click creates the matching source; nothing needs to change at the device.
strangers.title: Senders without a source

sources.testHelp: Puts a test message into the inbox as if it came from this source. Shows that nexsift works, but does not replace the test at the real sender.
sources.testSent: The test message is in the inbox.
sources.title: Sources
sources.unrecognizedHelp: The messages are there anyway, only without extras like bundling or the all-clear. Usually the sender changed its format with an update. "Raw data" in the message shows what arrived.
sources.unrecognized_one: The last message had an unknown format.
sources.unrecognized_other: The last {{count}} messages had an unknown format.

targets.chatIdHelp: The number of the chat or group. Easiest: write to the bot, then open https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates and read the "id" under "chat".
targets.help: Targets are where nexsift forwards what matters, usually the ntfy or Gotify app on the phone. Everything below the minimum level stays quietly in the inbox.

how.apprise: Apprise API: the address of an Apprise server with a key, like http://apprise:8000/notify/phone. Apprise spreads it further.
how.gotify: A real Gotify server with the Gotify app on the phone. Create an application there and enter its token here.
how.ntfy: The ntfy app on the phone, with ntfy.sh or your own ntfy server. Subscribe to a topic in the app and enter its full address here.
how.telegram: A Telegram bot writes to you. Create the bot with @BotFather, enter the token here, write to the bot once, then the chat ID.
how.webhook: Any service that takes JSON: nexsift POSTs title, message, priority and link.

targets.intro: Where nexsift sends what matters. Everything else stays quietly in the inbox.
targets.kindHelp: Which service delivers the pushes. If you already have the ntfy or Gotify app, take that.
targets.minPriorityHelp: Right for nearly everyone: only critical. Warnings then only land in the inbox.
targets.name: Name
targets.nameHelp: Free to choose, like "Phone" or "Family group".
targets.none: Nothing goes to the phone yet. Add a target; the ntfy app is the easiest.
targets.quietHelp: During this time only critical messages get through. Warnings and info do not wait; they simply stay in the inbox.
targets.testHelp: Sends a test message to this target right now.
targets.testOk: The test to {{name}} is out. Did it arrive?
targets.title: Forwarding to the phone

tokenHelp.gotify: In Gotify: Apps, Create application, copy the token.
tokenHelp.ntfy: Only needed if your ntfy server asks for a sign-in (tk_…). Leave empty for ntfy.sh.

urlHelp.apprise: The full address of the Apprise API endpoint, with the key.
urlHelp.gotify: The address of your Gotify server, without /message.
urlHelp.ntfy: Server and topic together, exactly as subscribed in the app. A long, random topic keeps others from reading along.

unreachable.lead: The interface cannot reach the nexsift server right now. After an update it is usually back within a minute; this page tries again every five seconds on its own.
unreachable.title: Server not reachable

welcome.keys: Tip: in the inbox everything works with the keyboard. The ? key shows how.
welcome.lead: nexsift gathers all your homelab's messages in one place, bundles the noise and only pushes what matters to your phone. This is how to start:

phone.text: Enter the ntfy or Gotify app on your phone as a target. From then on critical things arrive at once.
phone.title: Connect the phone

source.text: Watchtower, Proxmox, Uptime Kuma, Synology … The dialog shows exactly what to enter in the sender.
source.title: Add the first source

test.text: Trigger a test message in the sender. It shows up here at once.

welcome.title: Welcome to nexsift
